sections.title: Sound of the letter u
paragraphs: The letter name is (u) /y/. Its main sound appears in (usine) /y.zin/, which means factory. This letter makes two sounds. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. One sound is a full vowel, and the other is a fast glide.

sections.title: How to say u
paragraphs: Push your tongue forward behind your bottom teeth. Make a tight, small circle with your lips. Breathe out and turn on your voice. Place a finger across your lips to feel the small round circle. For the second sound, make the exact same shape. Then glide quickly into the next sound without stopping your voice.

sections.title: Spelling rules for u
paragraphs: As a regular vowel, this letter sounds like (sûr) /syʁ/. This happens in most positions, including under an accent mark. When it stands right before another pronounced vowel, it becomes a fast glide. You hear this shorter variant clearly in (nuit) /nɥi/. In (huit) /ɥit/, the same sound opens the word before another vowel.

sections.title: Common mistakes with u
paragraphs: Do not replace this sound with the vowel in boot. Pull your tongue forward instead of letting it rest back. Do not use the vowel in see either. Keep your lips pushed into a tight circle while saying that high sound. Never pronounce it like the w in wet. Your tongue must stay high and forward.
